channel_dna.platform_type: Real-time public microblogging and social network. Dominant for tech, media, finance, and startup discourse.
channel_dna.algorithm_type: Hybrid: For You Page (algorithmic, interest + engagement signals) + Following feed (chronological). Replies and quote tweets amplify reach. Early engagement in first 30 minutes determines algorithmic push. Replies from high-follower accounts to your content dramatically amplify reach.
channel_dna.primary_audience: Tech founders, VCs, journalists, developers, marketers, creators. 25-45 skew. Highly influential despite smaller size than Instagram/TikTok. 1 right tweet can reach millions.
channel_dna.native_content_formats: Short tweets (under 280 chars), long-form threads, image tweets, video tweets (under 2:20 for max reach), polls, quote tweets. Threads are the highest-engagement format for founders. Replies to large accounts are the highest-leverage discovery mechanism.
channel_dna.platform_culture_code: Build in public is the dominant founder culture. Opinions and hot takes get engagement. Data and receipts get respect. Authenticity over polish. The reply game matters MORE than original content — being seen in the comments of large accounts is how you grow. Being wrong publicly and owning it = massive respect.
channel_dna.account_warmup_requirements: No formal warmup required, but accounts with under 100 followers get minimal algorithmic reach. First 90 days are about presence and visibility through replies — original content comes second. Follower count matters for credibility at scale but not for early engagement strategy.

profile_setup.step_1_premium: Buy Twitter/X Premium (Blue checkmark). This is not optional for founders building in public. Premium gives you: algorithmic prioritisation in replies, longer posts, ability to edit tweets, and the verified badge which increases credibility significantly. Cost: $8-22/month depending on plan.
profile_setup.step_2_profile_photo: Use your real face as your profile photo. Not a logo, not an avatar, not an abstract illustration. Founders who build in public get dramatically higher engagement when people can see a real person behind the account. A clear, well-lit headshot or a photo of you working is ideal.
profile_setup.step_3_bio: Write a bio that clearly explains: who you are, what you are building, and what you talk about. Formula: '[Your role] building [Product] — [one-line description]. Writing about [topic areas].' Include your product URL directly in the bio URL field. Example: 'Founder building Farcast — AI growth agent for founders. Writing about distribution, GTM, and building in public.'
profile_setup.step_4_pinned_tweet: Pin a tweet that explains what you are building and invites people to follow the journey. This serves as a permanent landing page for anyone who visits your profile after seeing you in someone else's replies.
profile_setup.step_5_following_strategy: Follow 50-100 large accounts in your target niche immediately. These are the accounts whose reply sections you will be living in. For founder/SaaS audience: follow top indie hackers, SaaS founders, VCs, growth operators, and product builders with 10K-500K followers.

fit_scoring_matrix.best_product_types: B2B SaaS, developer tools, AI/ML products, creator economy tools, fintech, productivity apps. Any product where the founder IS the brand early on.
fit_scoring_matrix.worst_product_types: Local businesses, offline services, products targeting non-tech audiences 40+, highly regulated industries where public commentary is restricted.
fit_scoring_matrix.best_pricing_models: All models work. Freemium benefits most from Twitter virality. Paid products use Twitter for trust-building and credibility before conversion.
fit_scoring_matrix.icp_match_signals: Search your product category + 'tool' or 'app' on Twitter. If 10+ tweets per day mention your problem space, your ICP is active. Check if thought leaders in your space have 10K+ followers.
fit_scoring_matrix.red_flags_skip_this_channel: Skip if your ICP is non-English speaking or offline. Skip if you are unwilling to share opinions publicly. Skip if your product category has no active Twitter community.
fit_scoring_matrix.geographic_strength: US dominant (32%), UK (8%), Japan (8%), India (7%). Tech and startup discourse is English-language global.

growth_mechanics.expected_cac: $0 cash with organic strategy plus $8-22/month for Premium. Time cost: 5-7 hrs/week for real compounding growth — split roughly 60% replies, 40% original content.
growth_mechanics.time_to_first_traffic_spike: Can happen within hours if a reply to a large account gets significant engagement. Typically 2-4 weeks of consistent reply activity before algorithmic traction on original content begins.
growth_mechanics.time_to_first_paying_user: 3-6 weeks if building in public with product mentions. Faster if a high-engagement reply drives profile visits and the pinned tweet converts them.
growth_mechanics.effort_level: High. Twitter rewards daily presence. The reply game is 60% of the early strategy — you must engage with others consistently. Content half-life is 18-24 hours. Volume matters: 20+ replies per day is the target.
growth_mechanics.virality_coefficient: High. Retweets and quote tweets create exponential amplification. A reply to a viral tweet can get more impressions than most original tweets from new accounts.
growth_mechanics.compounding_potential: Low for individual tweets (expire in 24 hrs). High for reputation and followers — a well-built account compounds over years. The reply game builds recognition faster than original content in early days.

algorithm_playbook.how_reach_is_determined: Engagement rate in first 30 minutes (likes, replies, retweets, bookmarks). Reply engagement weighted most heavily — replies signal real conversation. Profile click-through rate influences future distribution. Accounts with Premium get slight algorithmic prioritisation in reply sections.
algorithm_playbook.what_algorithm_rewards: Threads with strong hook tweet. Replies that generate sub-conversations. Tweets that get bookmarked (save = high-value signal). Video content (2x organic reach vs text). Consistency — posting daily trains the algorithm. Replies from your account appearing under popular posts.
algorithm_playbook.what_kills_reach: External links in original tweet body (algorithm deprioritises — put links in first reply instead). Posting and not engaging for 24+ hours. Spammy follow/unfollow patterns. Quote tweeting yourself to boost. Excessive hashtag use (3+ hashtags = spam signal). Generic or sycophantic replies ('Great post!' adds nothing).
algorithm_playbook.peak_posting_windows: Tuesday-Thursday 8-10am EST for B2B/tech audience. Saturday morning for broader reach. Avoid Sunday evening and Monday morning.
algorithm_playbook.optimal_posting_cadence: 3-5 original tweets/day for growth phase. 1-2 threads/week. Minimum 1 tweet/day to maintain algorithmic presence. 20+ replies to other accounts daily — this is more important than original tweet volume at the early stage.
algorithm_playbook.content_freshness_window: Original tweets: 18-24 hours active. Threads: 24-48 hours. Replies can drive traffic to your profile for days if the parent tweet keeps getting engagement.

execution_sequence.phase_1_reply_guy: For the first 2-4 weeks, the primary activity is replies — not original content. Follow 50-100 large accounts in your niche. Every day, go through their latest posts and leave 20+ replies. Replies should be: (a) genuinely insightful, not generic, (b) quirky or take a clear position, (c) contrarian where you have a real different view, (d) affirmative with your own data or example added, (e) a hot take that adds a new dimension. The goal is to be seen consistently in the reply sections of accounts your ICP follows.
execution_sequence.phase_2_original_content: Once you have some follower momentum (even 50-100 engaged followers is enough), begin posting original content. But keep the reply-to-post ratio at 60:40 at minimum — more replies than original posts. Never stop the reply game even when you are posting regularly.
execution_sequence.phase_3_content_mix: Mature content mix: daily replies (20+), 3-5 original tweets per day (hot takes, observations, build-in-public updates), 1-2 threads per week (educational, story, lessons learned). Connect with relevant founders and indie hackers through genuine DMs after public interactions.

content_system.winning_content_types: 1. Build-in-public updates with real numbers (daily/weekly progress) 2. Hot takes on trends or news in your space — be the first to have an opinion 3. Educational threads ('Here is everything I know about X') 4. Behind-the-scenes product decisions with the reasoning 5. Personalised journey posts — specific moments from your week 6. Contrarian takes on conventional wisdom in your space 7. Replies to trending discussions that position your expertise
content_system.hook_formulas: Specific number: '18 months ago I had 0 users. Here is every mistake I made growing to 10K.' | Counterintuitive: 'Stop spending money on ads. You don't have a traffic problem, you have a conversion problem.' | Strong opinion: 'Cold email is dead. Here is what actually works in 2025.' | Story opener: 'At 2am last Tuesday, I got an email that changed everything.' | Trend angle: '[News/trend] just happened. Here is what this means for founders building in [space].'
content_system.reply_content_rules: Replies must add genuine value to be worth writing. Options: (1) Share a specific data point or personal experience that supports or challenges their point. (2) Take a clear position — agree or disagree with a reason, not just 'great take'. (3) Ask a specific follow-up question that shows you actually read the post. (4) Add a related insight they didn't mention. (5) Share a contrarian angle respectfully. Generic affirmations ('So true!', 'Great post!', 'This!') are invisible and waste your time.
content_system.platform_native_tone: Direct, opinionated, conversational. First person always. Short sentences. Punchy. Vulnerability is a superpower. Data beats vague claims. Humour works when authentic. No corporate speak ever.
content_system.personalisation_layer: The best performing posts reference specific personal moments — a real user conversation from this week, a specific metric from your product, a decision you made and why, something that surprised you in the last 7 days. Generic advice gets scrolled past. Specific personal experience stops scroll.
content_system.cta_approach: For product promotion: mention naturally in build-in-public updates. Put links in first reply, not tweet body. One clear CTA per thread (end of thread). Never make every tweet about the product — 80% value, 20% product.
content_system.content_to_avoid: Inspirational quotes without original thought. 'Retweet if you agree' engagement bait. Vague threads with no real content. Copying viral tweet formats without authenticity. Excessive self-promotion. Tweeting the same point repeatedly. Generic replies that don't add anything ('So true!', 'Love this').
content_system.cross_posting_rules: LinkedIn content can be adapted but must be reformatted — LinkedIn tone is too formal for Twitter. TikTok scripts can become Twitter threads. Never auto-post from one platform to another — native tone is critical.

community_outreach_playbook.where_icp_clusters: Identify 20-50 large accounts your ICP follows. These are your primary reply targets. Create a private Twitter List of these accounts to monitor their posts daily. Hashtags: #buildinpublic #indiedev #saas #founder for builder communities. Search for problem keywords to find people actively expressing pain.
community_outreach_playbook.contribution_before_pitch_rule: Spend first 2-4 weeks only replying and adding value to others' tweets. Never mention your product in someone else's replies until you have an established presence. Add genuine insights, not generic affirmation. 20+ replies per day is the target.
community_outreach_playbook.dm_outreach_approach: Only DM after 2+ meaningful public tweet interactions. Never cold DM with product pitch. DM template: 'Loved your thread on [topic] — [specific insight from the thread]. Building something related. Would love your feedback if you have 10 minutes.' Keep under 3 sentences. High reply rate when preceded by genuine public interaction.
community_outreach_playbook.influencer_partner_strategy: Target accounts with 5K-50K followers in your niche — they have engaged audiences and reasonable response rates. Engage consistently with their content for 2-3 weeks through replies before any outreach. Offer to share data, a guest thread, or a collaboration.
community_outreach_playbook.broadcast_vs_community_mode: Both, but with the reply game as the primary community mechanism. Broadcasting (original tweets/threads) builds audience. The reply game generates 30-40% of profile visits for active accounts and is the fastest path to early followers.
community_outreach_playbook.banned_behaviours: Buying followers (destroys engagement rate). Follow/unfollow bots. DM blasting product links. Coordinated inauthentic behaviour. Posting misleading data. Generic sycophantic replies at scale.

business_stage_playbook.pre_launch_0_users: Start with the reply game immediately — before you have anything to launch. Tweet about the problem you are solving, your research process, early mockups. Ask for feedback. Build an audience who is invested in your journey before you ask them to use or buy anything. Pin your 'I am building X because Y — follow the journey' tweet.
business_stage_playbook.early_traction_1_to_100: Tweet every milestone — first user, first paying customer, first churn, first bug. Be transparent about numbers. Ask followers to roast your landing page. Share DMs from users (with permission). This stage is about building trust through radical transparency. Keep the reply game going daily.
business_stage_playbook.growth_100_to_1k: Shift to educational threads that position your expertise. 'We grew to 500 users without ads — here is exactly what we did.' User case study threads. Start building an email list from Twitter — conversion asset you own.
business_stage_playbook.scale_1k_plus: Leverage social proof — user testimonials, revenue milestones. Collaborate with complementary product accounts. Consider Twitter Ads to amplify best-performing organic content. Build a team voice — not just founder account.

proof_of_play.early_stage_win: Levels.io (Pieter Levels) — built Nomad List, Remote OK, and multiple other products entirely through Twitter build-in-public strategy. Zero paid ads. $4M+ ARR built through Twitter audience of 450K followers over 8 years. Started as a constant presence in reply sections of other builders.
proof_of_play.growth_stage_win: Beehiiv — grew from 0 to $6M ARR partly through aggressive founder Twitter presence and build-in-public content sharing user growth milestones and product decisions publicly.
proof_of_play.what_made_it_work: Both treated Twitter as a trust-building platform, not a promotion platform. Both were heavy reply guys before they became known for original content. The product was a natural extension of the narrative they were already sharing publicly.
proof_of_play.what_would_have_killed_it: A Twitter presence consisting entirely of 'New feature launched — link in bio' posts would have zero engagement and zero conversions. A presence with only original content and no replies would grow 5x slower.
